resources.string: Optional. A cookies.txt exported from a browser where you are signed in to YouTube. It can help when YouTube asks to confirm you are not a bot. Use a secondary account: automated use may restrict an account. The file stays private to this app.
That file does not look like a cookies.txt with YouTube or Google cookies.
YouTube asked to confirm you are not a bot. Try again later or on another network, or import cookies in Settings.
Use a secondary YouTube account, not your main one. Automated requests can lead YouTube to restrict an account.
Cookies work like a login: anyone with the file can use that session. The app keeps it in private storage. Never share it, and remove it here when you no longer need it.

Export them from a private window so they do not expire: sign in to YouTube in a private or incognito window, open youtube.com/robots.txt in that same tab, export the youtube.com cookies with a cookies.txt extension, then close the window without signing out. YouTube rotates the cookies of open sessions, so a file taken from your everyday browser expires quickly.

The format must be Netscape HTTP Cookie File, not JSON. A known Chrome extension is Get cookies.txt LOCALLY and a Firefox one is cookies.txt. Some extensions have been removed or changed owner, so be wary of unknown ones.
The app updates the file as it uses it (yt-dlp rewrites it), so it can end up very different from the original. Keep a copy, and export it again if it stops working.
